The BaseMind Field Manual

Everything about the app a Scout group runs on — what each screen does, how the pieces fit together, how to stand a copy up from nothing, and where the sharp edges are.

Commit 3cb1629 · master Verified 27 August 2026 Screens live app, sample data

01 What BaseMind is

BaseMind is a web app for the day-to-day administration of one Scout group. It answers the questions a quartermaster and a camp leader actually ask:

  • What kit do we own, what condition is it in, and which room is it in?
  • Who has borrowed what, and when is it due back?
  • What camps are coming up, and where are they?
  • What do we need to pack, what do we need to eat, and what do we still need to buy?
  • Where is the nearest hospital to this site, and who is the first aider?
  • What do our group's own written policies say about this?

It is a rebuild. The original attempt tried to do everything at once and collapsed; this version started as equipment tracking plus roles, on Supabase, with access enforced by Postgres Row Level Security, and has grown one working feature at a time.

Design commitments

Four ideas run through the whole codebase, and most of the code makes more sense once you know them.

CommitmentWhat it means in practice
The database is the authorityA Viewer cannot write, even by calling the Supabase REST API directly with a valid token. Hidden buttons are a convenience, not the control.
It has to work at campTables are cached in IndexedDB, the shell is precached by a service worker, adds are queued offline and replayed, and the profile survives a dead connection so a leader isn't bounced to a login screen when the safety plan is needed.
A model's output is checked, not trustedBoth AI features verify the reply against the source data and discard it if it doesn't match. Every AI feature has a working non-AI path.
Nothing is inventedThe safety plan renders only facts that were typed in. The assistant answers only from uploaded documents, and every quote is looked up in the document before it is displayed.

02 A tour of the app

Signing in

Registration always creates a Pending / Viewer account regardless of what the browser sends — role and status are hard-coded in a database trigger, so self-registration cannot grant itself access. A new account lands on the pending screen until an Admin approves it.

Equipment

The default landing page. Items are grouped by room, with a count, a total quantity, and a badge for anything needing attention.

Borrowing

Loans record who took it, from which Scout group, their position and contacts, when it went out and when it's due. A loan with no returned_on is still outstanding.

Status is worked out in src/lib/loans.ts by comparing yyyy-mm-dd strings rather than Date objects — they sort correctly as text and it sidesteps a timezone shifting a due date by a day. An item is due soon within DUE_SOON_DAYS (3) of its due date. Quantities on loan are subtracted from the equipment list's availability, clamped at zero so a miscount shows 0 rather than a negative.

Camps

Three things in that screen are worth pointing out.

  • Condition travels with the packing list. A Needs Repair or Broken item shows its badge here, so it's visible at packing time rather than at camp.
  • Other camps' claims are subtracted. [sample] Bread shows "4 claimed by [sample] Weekend Patrol Camp". Without this, two camps a fortnight apart would each see the full cupboard and neither shopping list would mention the bread the other is taking.
  • The shopping list is derived, never typed. It is the food plan filtered to lines where toBuy > 0, where toBuy = needed − (inStock − claimedElsewhere).

Camping sites

Beyond contact details, each site carries what a safety plan needs: nearest hospital, its phone and address, how far it is, emergency vehicle access, and free-text emergency notes.

Forms

Food and menus

The food store is a plain inventory in whatever units suit — kg, tins, litres, packets, loaves. Menus are meal plans: meals per day, ingredients per meal, written for a stated number of people. A menu with event_id = null is a reusable preset; one with an event_id belongs to a camp. Applying a preset scales every quantity by headcount / serves.

Two documented rules, visible above

Neither menu screen shows a "Food store / Menus" tab strip, even though MenusPage renders one. Food is switched off in this project, which leaves the strip with a single tab — and a lone tab renders nothing. The section itself survives in the nav because Menus, its other tab, is still on.

aggregateMenuRequirements sums the same ingredient across every meal that uses it — rice at lunch on day one and dinner on day two is one line on the shopping list, not two — and mergeRequirements folds in anything added by hand on the event. Two Postgres functions do the copying server-side so it is atomic: apply_menu_preset and save_menu_as_preset.

Assistant

Conversations are saved and private to whoever asked — enforced by row-level security on policy_chats, not just by the UI. Only the last three exchanges are replayed to the model: enough for a follow-up like "and what about cubs?" without pushing the documents down a prompt that grows every turn.

Admin and users

Making both directions equally hard would just train people to click through. The data is untouched either way. A route whose feature is off renders this rather than 404ing:

Dark mode and mobile

The theme is a class on <html>, persisted to localStorage. Every colour is a CSS variable, including the eight person-icon hues, so they swap together.

On a phone the header nav is hidden and a fixed bottom bar takes over — four wide targets that are easier to reach one-handed than a row that scrolls off the edge.

03 Roles and permissions

Four roles and three account statuses.

status:  Pending  →  Active     (an Admin approves)
                  →  Rejected   (an Admin rejects, or later deactivates)

role:    Viewer   (the default every new account gets)
         Member
         Manager
         Admin

Only an Active account can do anything at all. Pending and Rejected accounts fail is_active_user() in every policy, so they are blocked at the database, not merely redirected.

CapabilityAdminManagerMemberViewer
Read everything✓✓✓✓
Add / edit equipment, camps, sites, food, menus, loans, forms✓✓✓—
Delete those✓✓——
Add / edit / delete policy documents✓✓——
Ask the assistant✓✓✓✓
Approve signups, change roles, deactivate✓———
Toggle feature switches✓———
The one asymmetry that matters

Only Admins and Managers can change policy documents, even though Members can edit everything else. An answer is only as trustworthy as who can edit what it answers from.

Own-row exceptions. Anyone can read and update their own users row — name, phone, icon choice — but a trigger reverts any attempt to change their own role or status. Chats are stricter still: a chat and its messages are visible only to the person who owns them, whatever their role.

04 Architecture

Stack

LayerChoice
UIReact 18.3, TypeScript 5.4
BuildVite 6.4, vite-plugin-pwa 0.21
StylingTailwind CSS v4, CSS variables for theming
ComponentsRadix UI primitives in the shadcn/ui pattern, lucide-react
RoutingReact Router 7.18, createBrowserRouter
BackendSupabase — Postgres, Auth, RLS, Realtime, Storage, Edge Functions
PDFsjspdf to write, pdf-lib to fill, pdfjs-dist to read — all lazy

There is no state-management library, no data-fetching library and no test framework. State lives in five context providers and one reusable realtime hook.

The provider stack

ThemeProvider              light/dark class on <html>, persisted
 └── (missing env vars? → render the config screen instead of the app)
     └── OfflineProvider   online/offline, the outbox, sync on reconnect
         └── AuthProvider  session, profile, role checks, cached fallback
             └── FeaturesProvider  the feature_flags table, live
                 └── RouterProvider + Toaster

The ordering is load-bearing. AuthProvider sits inside OfflineProvider because the cached profile is what keeps an already-signed-in leader from being bounced to the login screen with no signal. FeaturesProvider sits inside AuthProvider because reading feature_flags requires an active session.

If either environment variable is missing, the whole router is replaced by a screen naming what's absent. The Supabase client falls back to a dummy URL, because createClient throws on an empty one and that would blank the page before React could explain anything.

Routing

The three auth pages are eagerly loaded — they're the first thing anyone sees, so splitting them would only add a spinner to the critical path. Everything behind the login is lazy, which keeps the initial download small on a phone with camp-grade signal.

AppLayout is the real access gate: no session → /login; no profile or status !== "Active" → /pending.

Worth knowing

/equipment has no feature gate on the route, even though an equipment flag exists. Turning that flag off removes the Inventory tab and the section link, but the route still renders — and / still redirects to it.

Navigation structure

Four sections in the bar, not eight destinations — eight items never fitted a phone. Related pages are tabs within a section.

SectionTabs
EquipmentInventory /equipment, Borrowed /loans
CampsCalendar /events, Sites /sites, Forms /forms
FoodFood store /food, Menus /menus
AssistantAsk /assistant, Documents /policies

A section's tabs are its source of truth: it survives as long as any one of them is switched on, and points at the first one that is. Gating a section on a single feature meant turning off Food also hid Menus, which sits in the same section but has its own switch. A strip with one remaining tab renders nothing. Admin is deliberately not in this bar — settings live in the header, never pushed into an overflow menu.

The realtime data pattern

Almost every page uses one hook:

const { rows, loading, error } = useRealtimeTable("events", { orderBy: "start_date" });
  1. Reads the last known rows from IndexedDB and renders them immediately. At camp this is often the only data there is, and even on a good connection it beats a spinner.
  2. Fetches from Supabase, sorts, renders, writes the fresh copy back to IndexedDB.
  3. Subscribes to postgres_changes and folds INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE into local state.
  4. Suppresses the fetch error entirely if there was a usable cache — the offline banner already explains the situation.
The consequence to internalise

Mutations do not update local state. They write to Supabase per row and let the realtime event come back and do it. That's what keeps two leaders' tabs in step, and it's what the old app got wrong with whole-table rewrites.

Recovering from a deploy that lands mid-session

A real failure mode for a long-lived tab: the app is code-split into chunks whose filenames contain a build hash, so after a deploy an open page still refers to the previous build's filenames — and those are gone. The next navigation throws Failed to fetch dynamically imported module and the app falls over.

  • installStaleBuildHandler() listens for unhandledrejection and error, catching failures outside React's error boundary — a hover-triggered prefetch, or a lazy import that rejects between renders.
  • RouteError catches the same thing inside the router.
  • Recovery is a single reload, recorded in sessionStorage, so a genuinely broken build shows a real error instead of reloading forever.
  • The service worker uses skipWaiting, clientsClaim and cleanupOutdatedCaches, so the new build takes over immediately.

05 The data model

Eighteen tables. Every one has RLS enabled. Fifteen are in the supabase_realtime publication — the exceptions are users, policy_chats and policy_chat_messages, none of which benefit from being broadcast. 

auth.users ──(trigger)──▶ public.users
                             │
                             ├── equipment.checked_by
                             ├── policies.created_by
                             └── policy_chats.user_id ──▶ policy_chat_messages.chat_id

equipment ──▶ equipment_loans          (who has what, and when it's due)
          └──▶ event_equipment ◀── events            (the packing list)

camping_sites ◀── events ──▶ event_food ──▶ food_items   (the food plan)
      │              │
      │              ├──▶ menus ──▶ menu_meals ──▶ menu_meal_items ──▶ food_items
      │              └──▶ safety_plans ──▶ safety_scenarios
      └── hospital_*, emergency_* columns feed the safety plan

camp_forms          (an uploaded fillable PDF + its field mapping)
feature_flags       (the switches on the admin page)
policies            (documents + extracted text)
TableMigrationWhat it holds
users0001Profile mirror of auth.users: name, phone, role, status, icon choice
equipment0001Name, category, quantity, location, condition, notes, check dates
camping_sites0003, 0006Venue contacts; hospital and emergency fields added in 0006
events0003, 0005Camps, hikes, meetings; headcount added in 0005
event_equipment0003The packing list — event ↔ equipment with a quantity
food_items0003The food store: name, unit, quantity, category
event_food0003Food required for an event
equipment_loans0004Borrower, group, contacts, dates; returned_on null = still out
menus0005event_id = null → reusable preset; otherwise a camp's own menu
menu_meals0005Day number, meal slot, name, notes
menu_meal_items0005Ingredient lines: meal ↔ food item + quantity
safety_plans0006Leader, standby, first aider, emergency numbers, generated text
safety_scenarios0006Per-situation response, destination, contact, sort order
camp_forms0007Uploaded PDF's storage path + field_map
feature_flags0008, 0009Nine switches, keyed by key rather than id
policies0009, 0011Title, category, storage path, extracted content, source URL
policy_chats0011One saved conversation, owned by a user
policy_chat_messages0011Turns within a chat; assistant rows carry the verified result

Conventions

  • Primary keys are uuid, except users.id (references auth.users) and feature_flags.key (text).
  • updated_at is maintained by a shared trigger, not by the client.
  • Calendar dates are date, compared as yyyy-mm-dd strings in the app to avoid timezone drift.
  • Quantities go through roundQuantity() wherever they're summed, to shake off artefacts like 0.30000000000000004.
A trap in the type definitions

Row types must be type aliases, never interface. Supabase's client generic constrains every row to Record<string, unknown>, and an interface has no implicit index signature — using one silently degrades every insert/update argument to never.

06 The security model

This is the part the rebuild exists for, so it's worth reading properly.

Signup cannot elevate itself

handle_new_user() is an after insert trigger on auth.users. It creates the profile row with role and status hard-coded to 'Viewer' and 'Pending', ignoring anything the client put in its signup metadata. There is deliberately no INSERT policy on public.users — the trigger is security definer and bypasses RLS; client inserts are default-denied.

Two helper functions decide everything

public.current_role()    -- the caller's role, or NULL
public.is_active_user()  -- true only when the caller's status is 'Active'

Both are security definer and stable. That matters: they must bypass RLS internally, otherwise querying users from inside a policy defined on users recurses.

The standard policy shape

select  →  is_active_user()
insert  →  is_active_user() and current_role() in ('Admin','Manager','Member')
update  →  is_active_user() and current_role() in ('Admin','Manager','Member')
delete  →  is_active_user() and current_role() in ('Admin','Manager')

Deviations from that shape, all intentional:

TableDeviation
usersselect: own row or any active user. update: own row or an Admin. delete: Admin only. No insert policy.
policiesinsert/update/delete require Admin or Manager — Members cannot change what the assistant answers from.
feature_flagsselect: any active user (the nav needs them). update: Admin only. No insert or delete — the set of features is defined by migrations.
policy_chats, policy_chat_messagesScoped to user_id = auth.uid() for every operation, regardless of role. Messages check ownership through their parent chat.

Column-level protection for role and status

RLS's WITH CHECK can gate a whole row but not individual columns. A user allowed to update their own row could therefore set role = 'Admin' themselves. A trigger closes that: 

if auth.uid() is not null and public.current_role() is distinct from 'Admin' then
  new.role   := old.role;
  new.status := old.status;
end if;

The auth.uid() is not null check is the subtle part, and is the entire subject of migration 0002. Statements from the SQL Editor carry no JWT, so auth.uid() is NULL and current_role() returns NULL — "distinct from Admin" — and without this guard the documented first-admin bootstrap would report success while silently changing nothing.

Storage

BucketCreated inReadWriteDelete
camp-forms0007any active userAdmin / Manager / MemberAdmin / Manager
policies0009any active userAdmin / ManagerAdmin / Manager

Migration 0010 removes an older avatars bucket entirely — person icons are drawn by the app, so nothing needs uploading.

The check that actually matters

Sign in as a Viewer, take that session's token, and POST directly to the Supabase REST equipment endpoint, bypassing the UI entirely. Postgres rejects it. That is the server-side enforcement the original app never had.

07 Offline behaviour

Three separate mechanisms, each covering a different failure.

1 · The app shell

Every JS, CSS, HTML, SVG and WOFF2 asset is precached — the size cap is raised to 5 MB because pdf-lib alone is ~440 kB and the default 2 MB cap would skip it. Supabase requests are explicitly NetworkOnly: data is cached by the app in IndexedDB, not by the service worker, and serving a stale auth round-trip would be actively harmful.

2 · Reading

useRealtimeTable caches each table in IndexedDB and renders from it first. AuthProvider caches the profile and falls back to it when the server can't be reached — so an already-signed-in leader with no signal stays signed in. The cached role decides what the UI offers, never what the database allows.

3 · Writing

An outbox in IndexedDB. addRow() inserts directly when online; when offline — or when the error looks like a network failure rather than a rejection — it queues. On reconnect it waits a second for the connection to settle, then replays. Genuine rejections (RLS, constraint violations) surface immediately rather than being queued to fail again later; permanently failed rows are surfaced so they aren't lost silently. 

canAdd    = Admin | Manager | Member          // allowed offline: queued and replayed
canEdit   = (Admin | Manager | Member) && online
canDelete = (Admin | Manager) && online

The split is deliberate. Adding queues safely — two people adding different rows never collide. Editing or deleting the same row does collide, and resolving that without asking would mean quietly discarding someone's work. So those are paused until there's a connection to check against, and blockedByOffline tells the UI to explain that rather than just hiding the button.

Failing open

isEnabled() returns true for any flag it doesn't have. If the flags table can't be read — offline before it was ever cached, or migration 0008 not yet run — hiding the whole app would be far worse than showing a section someone turned off.

08 The AI features, and how they're constrained

Two optional features use Gemini. Both work on the same principle: the model's instruction not to invent things is not trusted; its output is verified against the source data and discarded if it doesn't match. Both have a fully working non-AI path.

The API key never reaches the browser. It lives as a Supabase Edge Function secret; a VITE_ variable would be baked into the bundle and readable by anyone who opens devtools.

FunctionSecretsWithout it
safety-planGEMINI_API_KEYThe "Rewrite more readably" button errors; the template still works
policy-chatGEMINI_API_KEYDocuments still upload, search and open; only the question box errors
fetch-policy-pdfnoneUploading files still works; only "add by link" is unavailable

Both AI functions default to gemini-3.5-flash-lite — the cheapest class with the most generous free quota, and its thinking level already defaults to minimal so none of the output budget goes on reasoning. Override with a GEMINI_MODEL secret. If the name isn't available on your key the call fails with a 404, and the error names both the model it tried and lists the models your key can actually use.

Deployed by hand

These functions do not update from a git push. After editing one in the repo you must paste it into the Supabase dashboard again.

Safety plans

collectFacts() flattens everything a leader typed, plus the site's emergency fields, into labelled pairs. That single list is both what the deterministic template renders and what any generated prose is checked against — so the two cannot drift apart.

The optional rewrite is constrained three ways:

  1. The key is server-side.
  2. The model is told to use only the supplied facts.
  3. Every number in the reply is checked against the facts before it's shown. A reply containing an unrecognised number is discarded and you keep the plain version.

safety_plans.generated_by records 'template' or 'gemini' so you can always tell which you're looking at. Whatever produced it, read the plan before you rely on it.

The assistant

Getting text in. Text is extracted from a PDF with pdf.js (lazy-loaded — ~350 kB, only needed when someone adds a document). Incidental PDF spacing is collapsed, because citations are later matched against this stored text. A PDF yielding no text — a scan or a photograph — is rejected at upload with an explanation, rather than silently becoming a document that never appears in any answer.

Replacing, not duplicating. A document whose title you already have replaces the existing one; a unique index on lower(title) enforces it. Two copies means the assistant quotes whichever it read first, and an edit to one silently doesn't apply.

Adding by link. fetch-policy-pdf downloads server-side, because almost nothing serves a PDF with headers that allow a cross-origin read — and because at camp the user's connection is the one you least want to spend on a 4 MB file. It's fetching a URL somebody typed, from inside your infrastructure, which is the classic shape of a server-side request forgery, so it:

  • accepts only http/https
  • requires the caller to be an Active Admin or Manager, checked against the database
  • follows redirects by hand, re-checking the destination at every hop (max 3)
  • refuses loopback, private, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses
  • requires the response to actually be a PDF, capped at 15 MB

The file's own comments name the residual risk honestly: a public hostname that resolves to a private address (DNS rebinding) isn't caught, because name resolution isn't available there to check.

Verifying answers

This is the core of it. The model returns an answer plus citations, each naming a policy and quoting it verbatim. Then verifyAnswer():

  1. Resolves each citation's policy by id, falling back to a normalised title match.
  2. Looks the quote up in that policy's stored text.
  3. Drops anything that fails, into a rejected list with a reason.
  4. De-duplicates repeated quotes.
  5. Sets unsupported when the answer made claims but none could be traced to a policy.

Matching is whitespace- and case-insensitive but keeps punctuation — PDF extraction introduces line breaks and runs of spaces that don't exist in the sentence a reader sees, so an exact match would reject honest quotes, while dropping punctuation would let meaningfully different text match. Quotes shorter than 12 characters are never accepted: they match by accident and are evidence of nothing.

Why discard rather than flag

A citation nobody can follow is worse than no citation, because it looks authoritative. The same check runs in the Edge Function and again in the browser.

Saying "not covered". The model returns a covered flag and, when false, questions the documents can answer. That flag is optional in the type — a browser may be talking to an older hand-deployed function that never sends it, and a missing flag therefore means "work it out from the prose", not "not covered".

Chats. Nothing is written until an answer actually arrives, so a failed question leaves no half-conversation behind.

09 PDFs and form filling

ConcernLibraryWhere
Writing a camp plan / menujspdf + jspdf-autotablelib/campPlanPdf.ts, lib/menuPdf.ts
Filling an existing fillable PDFpdf-liblib/formFill.ts
Reading text out of a PDFpdfjs-distlib/documentText.ts

The camp plan assembles the event, its site (contact details included), the menu days, the packing list, the food plan and the shopping list into one printable document. Filenames are slugged: camp-plan-<slug>-<start-date>.pdf.

Form filling. Upload an official fillable PDF once. BaseMind reads its field names and you map each to a data key — event.date_range, hospital.phone, safety.leader_in_charge, safety.full_text (the whole rendered plan), today. The mapping lives in camp_forms.field_map.

Maintenance note

These keys are stable strings stored in the database. Renaming one orphans every existing mapping. Add new keys rather than changing old ones.

10 Person icons

Everyone gets a camp badge — one of sixteen emblems in one of eight colours, 128 combinations — shown in the header and anywhere people are listed. It is computed from the user's id in the browser, which is the whole point:

  • a new account has one immediately, with nothing to upload and nothing to set up
  • it is identical on every device
  • it still draws with no connection
  • there is no state in which somebody has no icon

Your profile → Your icon lets you pin an emblem and colour instead, or switch to your initials. Two nullable columns store that choice; "Start again" clears them and hands the choice back to your id. No image is uploaded, generated or hosted anywhere.

11 Feature flags

Nine switches, one row each. Rows rather than a single settings blob, so two admins toggling different things cannot overwrite each other.

KeyLabelGates
equipmentEquipmentThe Inventory tab (not the /equipment route)
loansBorrowing/loans
eventsCalendar/events, /events/new, /events/:id
sitesSites/sites
menusMenus/menus
foodFood/food
formsForms/forms
safetySafety plansThe safety plan section on the camp page
policiesPolicies/assistant and /policies

Changes propagate live over Realtime — no redeploy, no refresh. Turning something off hides its page and menu item for everyone; the data stays exactly where it is.

12 Setting it up from scratch

Prerequisites

  • Node.js 20 or newer, and npm
  • A Supabase account
  • Optionally, a Google AI Studio key for the two AI features

1 · Install

cd basemind-app
npm install

2 · Create a Supabase project

From Project Settings → API, note the Project URL and the anon / public key. The anon key is meant to be public — RLS is what protects the data, not key secrecy.

3 · Run the migrations

Open the SQL Editor and run everything in supabase/migrations/ in order, once each.

MigrationAdds
0001_init.sqlusers and equipment, the signup trigger, the RLS helpers
0002_fix_admin_bootstrap.sqlNothing on a fresh project — see the note inside the file
0003_camps_and_food.sqlCamping sites, events, packing lists, food store, camp food plans
0004_equipment_loans.sqlBorrowing
0005_menus.sqlMenus, meals, ingredients, event headcount, the two menu functions
0006_safety.sqlHospital/emergency fields per site, safety plans and scenarios
0007_camp_forms.sqlUploaded fillable PDFs, field mappings, the camp-forms bucket
0008_feature_flags.sqlThe eight original feature switches
0009_policies.sqlPolicy documents, extracted text, the policies bucket, the ninth switch
0010_user_icons.sqlThe emblem/colour columns; removes the old avatars bucket
0011_assistant_chats.sqlSaved chats and messages, policy source URLs, unique titles
The repo README is behind

basemind-app/README.md lists migrations only as far as 0010. 0011 exists and is required for the assistant's saved chats and for adding policies by link.

0002 and 0010 are safe to run twice; the rest are not. The calendar, sites and food pages will error until 0003 has been applied.

4 · Environment variables

cp .env.example .env.local
VITE_SUPABASE_URL=https://<your-project>.supabase.co
VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=<your anon key>

Both are required. Missing either replaces the app with a screen naming what's absent.

5 · Run it

npm run dev

Vite serves on port 5173 with --host, so it's reachable from a phone on the same network.

6 · Decide on email confirmation

Supabase turns Confirm email on by default. This app already gates access behind admin approval, so that step is mostly redundant friction for a small group. To turn it off: Authentication → Providers → Email → toggle off Confirm email. To confirm one manually: 

update auth.users set email_confirmed_at = now() where email = 'you@example.com';

7 · Create the first Admin

There is no admin yet to approve the first signup, so:

  1. Go to /register and create an account. You'll land on the pending screen.
  2. In the SQL Editor, with your own email, run the statement below.
  3. Sign out and back in. You'll land on Equipment with the admin gear in the header.
update public.users set role = 'Admin', status = 'Active' where email = 'you@example.com';

This touches public.users only — it does not confirm the email address. That's the separate auth.users step above.

8 · Optional: sample data

Run supabase/seed/dummy_data.sql to fill the app with fictional equipment across four rooms and six categories, four camping sites, a food store, and five events — two with full packing lists and food plans. Every row is prefixed [sample], and remove_dummy_data.sql removes all of it without touching anything you added. Every screenshot in this document is of exactly this seed data.

9 · Optional: the AI features

For each of the three functions in supabase/functions/: Supabase dashboard → Edge Functions → create a function with that exact name → paste the file's contents. safety-plan and policy-chat need a GEMINI_API_KEY secret; fetch-policy-pdf needs none. Skip any of them and the feature degrades to its non-AI path.

13 Deploying to Vercel

  1. Push to GitHub. Create the empty repo first, then push.
  2. Import into Vercel. vercel.json sets the build command, the output directory, and — importantly — a rewrite that serves index.html for every path. Without it, a client-side route like /events/abc 404s when someone reloads or opens a deep link.
  3. Set environment variables. VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY. These are read at build time, so redeploy after adding them if the first deploy already ran.
  4. Supabase Auth redirect URLs. If email confirmation is on, add your Vercel domain under Authentication → URL Configuration → Redirect URLs, or confirmation links bounce back to localhost. 
{ "rewrites": [{ "source": "/(.*)", "destination": "/index.html" }] }
If the repo root is the parent folder

Set Vercel's Root Directory to basemind-app so it finds vercel.json and package.json.

Order matters: get the Supabase project and schema done first, since the build needs those variables.

14 Verifying it works

  • npm run dev boots with no console errors and the purple theme applies.
  • npm run build completes — it runs tsc --noEmit first, so it fails on any type error.
  • Register a second test account, approve it as each role in turn, and confirm each sees exactly the controls its role allows.
  • A Viewer or Pending account cannot reach /users or /admin.
  • The real test: with a Viewer's session, make a direct write to the Supabase REST equipment endpoint, bypassing the UI, and confirm Postgres rejects it.
  • Two sessions as different Active users: edit equipment in one tab and watch it appear in the other without a refresh.
  • An Admin rejects a user → that account is immediately locked out.
  • Turn a feature off in Admin and watch the section disappear in the other tab, live.
  • Go offline in devtools, add an item, come back online, and watch the sync toast.

15 Troubleshooting

SymptomCause and fix
"Configuration missing" screenEnv vars unset. Locally, fill .env.local; on Vercel, add them and redeploy — they're read at build time.
Email not confirmed on sign-inSupabase's Confirm email is on. Click the link, turn it off, or set email_confirmed_at manually.
Stuck on "pending approval"No Admin has approved you. For the first account, run the bootstrap SQL in step 7.
Bootstrap SQL runs but changes nothingThe pre-0002 trigger silently reverting role/status for callers with no JWT. Run 0002_fix_admin_bootstrap.sql.
Calendar / Sites / Food pages errorMigration 0003 hasn't been run.
Admin says "No feature switches found"Migration 0008 hasn't been run. Everything stays on until it is.
Assistant errors on every questionpolicy-chat not deployed, or GEMINI_API_KEY not set. Documents still work.
Gemini 404 naming the modelGEMINI_MODEL isn't available on your key. The error lists the models that are.
Editing an Edge Function had no effectThey don't deploy from git. Paste the file into the dashboard again.
"No text could be read from that PDF"It's a scan or photograph — the pages are images. Export a text-based PDF from the original.
Deep link 404s on VercelThe rewrites rule isn't being picked up — check Vercel's Root Directory setting.
Failed to fetch dynamically imported moduleA deploy landed mid-session. The app reloads itself once automatically; seeing the error means that reload already happened.
Edit/delete buttons missing but add worksYou're offline. canEdit and canDelete require a connection by design.

16 Working on the code

npm run dev       # Vite dev server on :5173, exposed on the LAN
npm run build     # tsc --noEmit, then vite build → dist/
npm run preview   # serve the built output

There is no linter, formatter or test suite configured. npm run build is the gate — it type-checks the whole project before bundling.

Conventions worth matching

  • Comments explain why, not what. The existing comments are unusually good about naming the failure a piece of code exists to prevent. Match that.
  • Business logic goes in src/lib/, framework-free and independently readable. Components compose it.
  • Read through useRealtimeTable, write straight to Supabase. Don't update local state after a mutation — let the realtime event do it.
  • Row types are type aliases, never interface.
  • Never edit a migration that's already been run. Migration 0002's own comment calls out exactly this mistake having been made once already.
  • Path alias: @/ → src/.

17 Known gaps and things to watch

Honest notes, not criticisms — most are already acknowledged in the source.

  1. The equipment feature flag doesn't gate its route. Every other flag wraps its routes in RequireFeature; /equipment doesn't, and / still redirects there.
  2. The app README stops at migration 0010. 0011 exists and is required. Its closing "What's deliberately not here" section is also well out of date — it still says camp planning, documents and the chatbot are cut, and all three have since been built.
  3. Edge Functions are deployed by hand. There's no deploy step in any workflow, so the code in the repo and the code actually running can drift. The optional covered field exists precisely to tolerate that.
  4. DNS rebinding isn't covered by fetch-policy-pdf's SSRF guards, as its own comments state. Literal private addresses and metadata hostnames are blocked.
  5. No tests. tsc --noEmit is the only automated check. The pure-logic modules in src/lib/ are written as pure functions and would be straightforward to test — the obvious first place to start.
  6. A stale cached role widens the UI, not access. Worth restating because it looks alarming and isn't: RLS still runs server-side on every write.
  7. 0001_init.sql was edited after being run. Acknowledged in 0002's comments. A database created from the original 0001 needs 0002; one from the current 0001 doesn't, and running it anyway is harmless.
